A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CQN-AS by Seo and Abbeel. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison, including the HumanoidBench material relocated to an appendix in v4.

before.justification: V2 reports original CQN-AS experiments on BiGym, HumanoidBench, and RLBench, together with ablations and torque-control failure cases.

after.justification: V4 retains those original experiments and adds return-to-go prediction results and actor-critic episode-return diagnostics.

M1.justification: The written TD objectives change target conditioning from policy level l to l-1, including CQN-AS in v2 Equation 1 versus v4 Equation 2. This is a limited objective correction; the GRU architecture, coarse-to-fine inference, temporal ensemble, and replay procedures remain unchanged. An implementation change or rerun is not established.

E1.justification: The 53 BiGym, HumanoidBench, and RLBench control tasks and two DeepMind Control Suite failure cases remain. V4 adds an auxiliary return-to-go prediction task on five existing BiGym tasks. Moving HumanoidBench to Appendix A does not remove its coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain CQN, DrQ-v2+, and ACT for BiGym/RLBench, and CQN and SAC for HumanoidBench. The introductory diagnostic retains SAC, TD3, and their two- and four-step action-sequence variants.

E3.justification: V4 introduces a regression evaluation comparing action-sequence lengths 1 and 50 using validation L1 loss for discounted return-to-go prediction. It also reports episode return for the retained actor-critic Stand diagnostic. Existing benchmark budgets, observations, demonstration counts, and evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 adds the return-prediction analysis and actor-critic performance diagnostic in Figure 2a/c, while removing v2 Figure 1's trajectory visualizations and demonstration-smoothing replay analysis. The six component, sensitivity, and torque-control analyses are retained in v4 Figure 7.

E5.justification: The benchmark and ablation plots retain their mean/confidence-interval reporting and run counts: eight for BiGym and CQN/CQN-AS HumanoidBench experiments, four for RLBench and ablations, and three for sourced SAC results. No new seed, significance-testing, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: V4 Figure 2a newly reports five validation-L1 reductions for sequence length 50 versus 1, including 13.1% on Move Plate and 20.1% on Wall Cupboard Open. Figure 2c adds Stand episode-return curves. V2's smoothing-success results disappear; the matched benchmark and six ablation plots retain their results.

T1.justification: The level-index correction in the main text and mathematical appendix aligns target conditioning with the previously stated dependence on preceding-level actions. This changes the mathematical specification beyond equivalent notation. No new theorem, proof, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: V4 elevates lower return-prediction validation loss to an explicit contribution and focuses its abstract and introduction on demonstration-driven BiGym/RLBench results. The central CQN-AS contribution and claims of improvement over RL/BC baselines remain, while demonstration-free applicability is retained in Section 4.3 and Appendix A.

C2.justification: V4 explicitly identifies the absence of real-world robot evaluation as a limitation and interprets the new regression result through behavioral primitives. It also makes the temporal-ensemble mechanism explanation categorical where v2 called it a hypothesis, despite retaining the same ablation evidence.

D1.justification: The experimental appendix retains the task listings, hyperparameters, hardware, runtimes, implementation sources, and data-access pointers. The new regression probe does not receive architecture, validation-split, or optimization details that would substantially document its reproduction.

R1.justification: Section 5 substantially broadens positioning through new discussions of hierarchical RL/options and language-model multi-token prediction, including Gloeckle et al. and DeepSeek-V3. It explicitly distinguishes raw action-sequence value learning from hierarchical abstraction. Several earlier credit-assignment, exploration, and robotics references are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around the regression finding and an explicit contribution list, replacing the earlier credit-assignment opening. RLBench and HumanoidBench are reordered, HumanoidBench details move to Appendix A, and the conclusion becomes a discussion with explicit limitations.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with substantial resizing and relocation of displays. V4 replaces the old Figure 1 with a benchmark summary, combines the SAC/TD3 Q-value plots and adds diagnostic panels, revises the task montage, and moves HumanoidBench results to appendix Figure 8.

improvement.justification: V4 modestly improves motivation and precision through the new return-prediction and Stand-performance diagnostics, corrected conditioning indices, broader research context, and explicit real-world limitation. The principal benchmark evidence is preserved. Gains are limited by removal of the smoothing study and insufficient reproducibility details for the new regression analysis.
